test.name: Two bounded deliverables in one message are still bounded
test.description: Issue #2813 item 1. The bounded definition read "the message asks for ONE deliverable", so a message asking for TWO things that are each on the bounded list routed as a JOB. Reported in alpha feedback #3217, where the tester asked to evaluate a person's attached sources AND create a research plan. What that tester reported is the CLOSE, not dropped work: "instead of coming out and saying 'objective reached, do you want to move forward' it said 'do you want to move forward'". Here the message asks for a transcription AND a research plan, both on the list, so the turn is bounded. GRADING: deterministic, via `delivers:` rather than `routes-to:`. `routes-to:` asserts only the FIRST hand-off, so it passes a turn that delivers one deliverable and silently drops the other, which IS the pre-change behaviour this test exists to catch; a blind review proved that by executing the validator. `test_every_bounded_deliverable_is_handed_off` requires a hand-off for every `delivers:` tag, in any order (the body imposes none), and requires the FIRST hand-off to be one of them, which is how the job path shows up: on a project with no questions the table's first satisfiable row sends you to question-selection. Every callee is stubbed, as in ut_research_020, so no agent runs for real; the test declares no mcp_fixtures and image_transcribe is not in LIVE_TOOLS, so an unstubbed image-reader would be spawned with no transcription tool. SCENARIO: blyeberg-first-plan, which already has ONE REGISTERED QUESTION and no plan, and that is load-bearing. On a zero-question project research-plan is unreachable: research/SKILL.md:201 says a stated question 'is not a question until' question-selection registers it, and ownership.json gives `questions` to question-selection alone, so the plan deliverable could only be reached through the very step this test calls the failure. A blind review caught that; the first draft used empty-project-just-created and was unsatisfiable.
